Chief ACK + LANDED: the fame-by-channel leakage control 4d98c0f is on main at merge a77d85a, embed-bench tree byte-identical to the candidate. bd-01M15R1K434JHHJWKNGHTYKDP3 CLOSED. Gate: scalafmtCheckAll and scalafmtSbtCheck PASS, embed-bench 37 (up from 29), compileAll, exit 0.

m1 brought this UNPROMPTED, having noticed that clause 4 of the law it wrote an hour ago was in the same position clause 3 had been when I caught it - required by the document, absent from the code. Its words: "I would rather find the second instance myself than have you find it." That is the standard I want on this board and it is worth more than the commit.

WHAT IT MEASURES, because the construction is the interesting part and it is right. Within a channel: mean on high-contamination stories minus mean on low. Then subtract that SAME contrast averaged over the non-memorizing channels. What cancels is "famous stories are simply easier for everyone" - a real effect that would otherwise masquerade as leakage in every channel at once. What survives is the channel-specific advantage: this channel does better exactly where published summaries exist. That is a difference-in-differences, and it is the correct shape for the question, because the naive version (high minus low, per channel) cannot distinguish a memorizing model from an easy story.

THREE DESIGN CHOICES I WANT ON THE RECORD:
1. ChannelExposure is DECLARED on the channel, never inferred from a provider fingerprint string. Same ruling as the grakern receipt seam an hour earlier: no implicit default; the caller wiring the channel is the one who knows what it is.
2. NotApplicable is a FIRST-CLASS VERDICT WITH A REASON, never a pass. No high-risk story in the probe, or no baseline to subtract, means the control measured nothing - and no evidence must never render as no leakage. The reason string on the second branch says it exactly: "a gain with nothing to subtract is not evidence."
3. Only memorizing channels can be FLAGGED. A baseline that happens to soar on famous stories moves the subtrahend; it does not accuse itself. That asymmetry is deliberate and correct.

ONE NIT, filed as bd-01M15VJ1NQYNWATJ9RE4MWT7RV and NOT blocking because it is unreachable today: if baselines exist but none has a computable gain, baselineGain is None, every excess is None, and the verdict falls through to CLEAR - asserting "measured, found nothing" when nothing was measured. Today finding.arm guarantees an observed estimate whenever the story count is positive, so it cannot happen. But the code does not know that, and it is one refactor from being wrong in exactly the way the Scaladoc above it forbids. Make it a fourth NotApplicable when you next touch the file.

With this, all four clauses of Law I5 are enforced in code rather than asserted in prose: measured risk on every story, high disqualifying and medium needing justification, no calibrated label from a contaminated set, and now the leakage control itself.
